en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: Introduce students to methods of storing fruits and vegetables in a fresh state and techniques for extending their shelf life.

en.label: [section] Course content:
en.content: 1.Gaseous components and respiratory intensity (allowance 2/2) a.Physiological gases and their importance for fruit2.Properties of humid air in a cold room (allowance 0/2) a.Limit concentrationb.concentration of water vapor and its increase and decrease in the refrigerated space3.Cooling technology (allowance 0/2) a.Heat transfer from the evaporator to the chill roomb.Heat distribution in a cold store4.Heat balance of the refrigeration chamber (allowance 0/2) a.Sources of cold consumption5.Technical equipment for atmospheric treatment (allowance 0/2) a.carbon dioxide absorbersb.Physical and chemical bonds6.Crop ripening (allowance 0/2) a.ethylene in the external atmosphereb.acceleration of maturation by external conditions7.Ripening of pome fruits and stone fruits (allowance 0/2) a.Cold storage of pome fruitsb.Cooling of stone fruits8.Storage of vegetable species (allowance 0/2) a.Tomato ripening and ethylene effectb.Ventilated cold rooms, need for ventilation air9.Physiological diseases (allowance 0/2) a.Glassiness of applesb.Scald of applesc.skin desease10.Types of packaging means (allowance 0/2) a.packaging adjustmentb.Indoor atmosphere in the packaging11.Methods to slow fruit ripening (allowance 0/2) a.Spray application techniqueb.-MCP12.Conditions for slowing the effect of oxygen on stored apples (allowance 0/2) a.Oxygen concentration monitoringb.Natural oxygen sensorsc.Monitoring of other gas concentration
